themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: The answer engine work notes that answers are stochastic and drift more than any intervention, the incrementality work says platforms control both treatment and evidence, identity resolution says nobody has a verified list of who is really the same person, and content review says expert reviewers themselves disagree.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blocker is often money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Today's semantic layer answers all three call conflicting definitions a political fight because teams are paid on different numbers, the agent traffic answers propose fast lanes and perks so declaring beats spoofing, and the journey orchestration answers say channel owners whose bonuses depend on volume will subvert any central arbiter.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: The agent execution answers all put a proxy or gateway in front of every write with hard spend and audience caps, the consent answers route every data export through a single checkpoint, and the orchestration answers add one shared contact log or pre-send eligibility check.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from the outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: The consent and deletion answers call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removing a person from a trained model, the incrementality answers say platforms conceal how treatment changes, and the agent execution answers say vendor APIs never expose the effects you need to predict.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: The content review answers limit generation to a registry of pre-approved claims because deciding whether evidence supports a claim stays a human call, and the semantic layer answers argue two teams can both be right about a term, so the goal is disclosing which definition was used rather than forcing one.
